title: GraphDistill-TI: A Temporal-Structural-Aware Data Distillation Framework for Fine-tuning Threat Intelligence LLMs
authors: Kaihua Zheng; Jianan Huang; Jinsheng Sun; Weiwei Liu
publication_title: 2025 International Conference on Cyber Resilience and Endogenous Safety & Security (CRESS)
abstract: The application of Large Language Models (LLMs) to Cyber Threat Intelligence (TI) is promising in automating and scaling threat analysis. However, their performance is often constrained by the immense volume and complex dynamics of TI data. Current data distillation techniques for fine-tuning, which primarily focus on local sample quality, largely ignore the global structural relationships and temporal evolution inherent in threat campaigns. This oversight leads to inefficient data utilization with an insufficient grasp of the macro-context, particularly the time-sensitive nature of threats. In this context, we propose GraphDistill-TI, a novel data distillation framework, which preserves the temporal and structural integrity of TI data for efficient LLM fine-tuning. GraphDistill-TI first constructs a temporal-structural threat graph, integrating semantic associations, explicit timestamps, and key entity labels from raw intelligence reports. Then, it employs a Graph Attention Autoencoder (GAT-GAE) to learn structural representations for each report. These representations facilitate a K-Means clustering that divides the data into structurally coherent groups, and in turn, guide a novel weighted greedy selection algorithm. This algorithm strategically selects a data subset by optimizing intra-cluster representativeness, inter-cluster diversity, and fidelity to a predefined Expected Temporal Distribution (ETD). Experiments on a real-world dataset containing 16,493 TI reports demonstrate that fine-tuning GPT-2 on a 10% subset distilled by GraphDistill-TI not only surpasses a full-dataset baseline in a threat intelligence question-answering task but also outperforms random 10% sampling by approximately 6.0%. Furthermore, ablation studies reveal and quantify a critical trade-off between structural purity measured by clustering metrics and temporal fidelity measured by Kullback-Leibler divergence. By strategically prioritizing temporal fidelity, GraphDistill-TI enhances model performance on dynamic and time-sensitive tasks. Through delicately balancing the priorities, GraphDistill-TI establishes a new paradigm for domain-aware data distillation and paves the way for more efficient and context-aware LLMs in cybersecurity applications.

abstract: The preservation of tacit knowledge in the manufacturing sector is becoming increasingly critical due to the rapid aging of the skilled workforce and the subsequent risk of skill loss. In this paper, we propose a multi-modal AI framework designed to automatically transform unstructured manufacturing videos into standardized digital manuals, referred to as “Know-how Heritage.” Unlike conventional video-to-text approaches, our system integrates Range of Motion (ROM) and Hand-Object Interaction (HOI) analysis to extract quantitative data on ergonomic postures and fine-grained tool manipulations. Large-scale experiments involving 3000 iterations on a shoe manufacturing dataset demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms baseline models, achieving a high Factuality score of 0.936 (G-Eval, 0-1 scale) and demonstrating superior structural coherence. This study provides a sustainable solution for digitizing industrial expertise, effectively bridging the gap between experts and the future workforce.

title: Radio Behavior Cognition: From Signal to Intention
authors: Yehui Song; Guoru Ding; Jiachen Sun; Yitao Xu; Fandi Lin; Peng Tang
publication_title: IEEE Network
abstract: As increasingly autonomous and intelligent electromagnetic devices become more integrated into various aspects of human life, there is growing pressure to recognize and manage their activities. Despite significant advancements in conventional radio frequency (RF) signal analysis, fully grasping the deep semantic information–namely, the intention behind signals–remains a challenge. To address this gap, we propose radio behavior cognition, a novel paradigm inspired by behavioral science, to interpret RF signals from a behavioral perspective. Specifically, we begin by investigating the trends in RF signal analysis and introduce the new concept of radio behavior. Next, we build the radio behavior cognition model to better analyze and understand radio behavior. Subsequently, we present a real-world case study on group communication behavior cognition for non-cooperative wireless networks, utilizing a large language model (LLM) to semantically interpret RF signals. Finally, open challenges and future directions are discussed.

title: DSM: Constructing a Diverse Semantic Map for 3D Visual Grounding
authors: Qinghongbing Xie; Zijian Liang; Fuhao Li; Long Zeng
publication_title: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Effective scene representation is critical for the visual grounding ability of reasoning. However, existing 3D Visual Grounding methods either only focus on geometric and visual cues, or like traditional 3D scene graphs, lack the multi-dimensional attributes needed for complex reasoning. To bridge this gap, we introduce a novel scene representation framework, Diverse Semantic Map (DSM), that enriches robust geometric map with a spectrum of VLM-derived semantics, including appearance, physical, and affordance attributes. The DSM is first constructed online by fusing multi-view observations within a temporal sliding window, creating a comprehensive map of scene knowledge. Building on this foundation, we propose a new grounding paradigm, DSM-Grounding, that shifts grounding from free-form queries to a structured reasoning process over the semantic-rich map for VLM. Extensive evaluations validate our approach's superiority, improving accuracy and interpretability. DSM-Grounding achieves a state-of-the-art 59.06% overall accuracy of IoU@0.5, surpassing others by 10% on ScanRefer. In semantic segmentation, our DSM attains a 67.93% F-mIoU, outperforming all baselines in Replica. Furthermore, successful deployment on physical robots for complex navigation and grasping tasks confirms the framework's practical utility in real-world scenarios.

abstract: This paper proposes a novel robotic manipulation framework named MA-OpenVLA, which significantly enhances the generalization capability and robustness of large-scale vision-language-action (VLA) foundation models in complex tasks by incorporating memory augmentation and continuous learning mechanisms. The framework adopts a dual-stream architecture: a Memory-Augmented Attention (MAA) pathway that retrieves and integrates past successful experiences from an external memory bank, and a base OpenVLA pathway that provides strong zero-shot generalization. title: TacMan-Turbo: Proactive Tactile Control for Robust and Efficient Articulated Object Manipulation
authors: Zihang Zhao; Zhenghao Qi; Yuyang Li; Leiyao Cui; Zhi Han; Lecheng Ruan; Yixin Zhu
publication_title: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Adept manipulation of articulated objects is essential for robots to operate successfully in human environments. Such manipulation requires both effectiveness—reliable operation despite uncertain object structures—and efficiency—swift execution with minimal redundant steps and smooth trajectories. Existing approaches struggle to achieve both objectives simultaneously: methods relying on predefined kinematic models lack robustness when encountering structural variations, while the tactile-informed approach achieves robust manipulation but sacrifices efficiency through reactive, step-by-step execute-and-recover cycles. To address this challenge, this paper introduces TacMan-Turbo, a proactive tactile control framework that unifies the cycles into a continuous control loop. Our key insight is to interpret tactile signals temporally in addition to spatially: instead of treating contact deviations merely as instantaneous error signals requiring immediate compensation, we analyze sequential tactile observations to reveal local kinematic information. This temporal perspective enables our controller to predict future object states and proactively modulate manipulation velocities, eliminating the previous execute-and-recover cycle. In evaluations across 200 diverse simulated articulated objects and real-world experiments, our approach maintains a near-perfect performance while significantly enhancing time efficiency, action efficiency, and trajectory smoothness (all p-values < 0.0001). These results demonstrate that tactile feedback serves a dual purpose: providing not only spatial error signals for reactive control but also critical temporal structural information that enables proactive prediction and control. By enabling robots to manipulate articulated objects both reliably and efficiently, this work advances robot capabilities for seamless operation in dynamic, human-centric environments. Note to Practitioners—Robots operating in human-centric environments need to adeptly manipulate articulated objects (e.g., drawers and doors), despite uncertain or inaccurate kinematic models, while finishing tasks quickly and smoothly without causing damage. Traditional planners that assume known kinematics are brittle in real-world settings, and recent tactile-reactive controllers, though robust, are slow due to repeated execute-and-recover cycles. TacMan-Turbo introduces a proactive tactile control framework built on a temporal interpretation of tactile signals: by extracting local kinematic information from sequential tactile observations, the controller predicts short-horizon handle motion and proactively adjusts end-effector velocity to track these predictions, eliminating dedicated recovery phases. In evaluations across 200 simulated articulated objects and real-world experiments, the method achieved near-perfect performance while reducing task completion time by nearly an order of magnitude compared to a strong tactile-based baseline, delivering higher action efficiency and smoother joint trajectories. Overall, TacMan-Turbo provides a training-free, drop-in upgrade for tactile manipulation of articulated objects, while preserving robustness and delivering faster, smoother, and more efficient operation without prior object kinematic models.

publication_title: 2025 China Automation Congress (CAC)
abstract: Robot end-to-end control frameworks face challenges in deployment cost, generalization, and flexibility. This paper proposes RAVES, a RAG-enhanced multi-agent collaborative control framework integrating three specialized agents (Perception, Decision, Feedback) based on large language models. The system implements distributed architecture with RAG technology for enhanced context and reasoning, achieving semantic mapping, task decomposition, and execution monitoring. Experiments on a six-DoF robotic arm demonstrate RAVES achieves 85.7% task success rate and 82.4% zero-shot adaptation, significantly outperforming traditional vision-guided grasping solutions. The system runs on consumer-grade hardware (RTX4060), handles complex manipulation tasks, and shows 3-4 orders of magnitude cost advantage compared to large model training approaches.

title: Semantic-Aware Robotic Grasping in Cluttered Environments via LLM and 3D Vision-Based Prediction
authors: Xiaohan Li; Zhejian Zhang; Siqi He; Shengjun Xu; Xunkai Wei; Hao Wang
publication_title: 2025 China Automation Congress (CAC)
abstract: Robotic grasping detection in unstructured environments remains a persistent challenge in dexterous manipulation systems due to the inherent complexity of partially observable scenes and semantic ambiguity. To address these issues, this paper proposes a 3D vision-based framework integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) with 6-DOF grasp prediction, enabling both general-purpose and task-specific grasping capabilities. Given an RGB image paired with a natural language instruction, the pre-trained LLM performs semantic parsing to extract high-level contextual cues and generates corresponding executable action sequences. Moreover, a dedicated high-confidence region detector is introduced to enhance spatial reasoning under cluttered and uncertain conditions. This network can estimate spatial graspability likelihoods to identify the topmost accessible object surfaces within complex object stacks. Furthermore, a direction-constrained 6-DOF pose generator is designed to formulate grasp candidates by coupling geometric feasibility with task context, followed by stability-optimized selection. Extensive experiments conducted in both simulation and real-world robotic setups demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, showing improved generalization across novel scenes and consistent performance gains in grasp success rates compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

title: Semantic-Aware Behavior Optimization With Safety Reinforcement Feedback for Language-Conditioned Manipulation
authors: Xiuxiu Qi; Jiannong Cao; Julie A. McCann; Chongshan Fan; Hanqian Luo; Hongpeng Wang
publication_title: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Language-conditioned manipulation (LCM) couples vision, language, and control to enable natural instruction following, making it a promising direction in embodied AI research. Researchers have combined imitation learning (IL) with reinforcement learning (RL), where IL provides sample-efficient initialization and RL refines the policy through feedback to maximize long-term returns. Despite progress, safe LCM execution faces two challenges: (1) a modality gap that disrupts semantic-spatial correspondence, degrading action quality, and (2) sparse safety costs in high-dimensional states that make constraint estimation and semantic–safety alignment difficult. In this paper, we present Semantic-Aware Behavior Optimization with Safety Reinforcement Feedback, a novel framework that mitigates multimodal misalignment through context-aware initialization and enforces semantic–safety consistency during execution. We introduce spatial–semantic priors to align language goals with spatial observations and embed safety cues. Specifically, a goal prior aligns modalities for context-aware initialization during behavioral cloning, while a constraint prior combined with a feasibility metric provides learnable supervision for safety reinforcement fine-tuning. Evaluations show our framework achieves a 6.7% relative improvement in simulation and effectively reduces safety violations in real-world tasks across diverse scenarios.

title: SGFAM: Semantic and Geometric Features Aggregation for Dense Shape Matching in Generalizable Robotic Manipulation
authors: Paolo Sebeto; Christian Hartl-Nesic; Jean-Baptiste Weibel; Daniel Zimmer; Andreas Holzinger; Markus Vincze
publication_title: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: To automate processes like polishing or cleaning at scale, robots must be able to adapt learned skills to new object instances without manual reprogramming. Applications requiring tool-surface interactions face a significant challenge in transferring manipulation strategies to novel objects due to substantial shape and appearance variations. Robust, generalized dense shape correspondence is essential for solving this problem. We present SGFAM, a zero-shot pipeline integrating pre-trained vision foundation models and geometric encoders via functional maps. Unlike prior works that rely on simple averaging, we introduce 1) an alignment-based feature aggregation to prioritize optimal viewing angles, and 2) Kernel PCA fusion to preserve non-linear descriptor manifolds. Our evaluations demonstrate that this approach not only outperforms state-of-the-art baselines but also enables lightweight vision backbones to achieve matching precision comparable to larger models. We validate SGFAM experimentally by successfully transferring continuous surface paths in real-world industrial and household robotic scenarios without requiring any finetuning.

title: LLM-Diffu: Robot Dexterous Grasp Generation Network With Diffusion Model and LLM
authors: Zhongli Wang; Pingyue Zhang; Shijie Guo; Haihang Wang; Yuanmin Dong
publication_title: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Generating accurate dexterous grasps for objects with complex geometries remains a critical challenge in robotic manipulation. The paper proposes LLM-Diffu, a novel network architecture built on the principles of diffusion models. This architecture integrates a specialized basis point set (BPS) point cloud encoder, a denoising network, and large language models (LLMs) to generate feasible, diverse, and high-quality dexterous grasps. For the dexterous hand grasp dataset, the paper proposes a method for constructing the dataset, which incorporates a multimodal large language model (MLLM) to enhance the grasp quality of the dataset and is applicable to the construction of various types of datasets. Simulated experiments show our LLM-Diffu outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving 79.6% and 83.2% grasp success rates on DexGraspNet and MultiDex datasets, respectively. Our constructed dataset has strong generalizability, supporting training of various dexterous grasp generation methods with promising results. Finally, real-world robotic experiments confirm the practical applicability of our constructed dataset.

title: AISPO: Enhancing Depth Reliability for Robotic Manipulation of Non-Lambertian Objects via Affine-Invariant Shape Prior
authors: Zhiming Chen; Linfang Zheng; Kun Zhang; Hyung Jin Chang; Wei Zhang; Hongyu Yu; Hua Chen
publication_title: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Reliable depth perception is critical for robotic manipulation, especially for non-Lambertian objects such as transparent or highly specular surfaces, where raw depth measurements are often corrupted or missing. These failures frequently propagate to motion planning, resulting in invalid grasp poses and execution errors. We propose AISPO, a depth completion framework that improves depth reliability for manipulation in challenging sensing conditions. AISPO combines multi-scale RGB-D feature fusion with an affine-invariant shape prior to enforce geometric consistency and mitigate catastrophic depth failures. Unlike methods that focus primarily on average depth accuracy, our approach emphasizes physical plausibility and structural integrity of the predicted depth maps. Extensive benchmark evaluations demonstrate competitive performance and strong generalization to unseen objects and novel scenes. Real-world grasping experiments further show that enhanced depth reliability significantly improves manipulation success rates, particularly for transparent objects where many existing methods fail to produce physically usable depth estimates.

title: Toward a Multi-Embodied Grasping Agent
authors: Roman Freiberg; Alexander Qualmann; Ngo Anh Vien; Gerhard Neumann
publication_title: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Multi-embodiment grasping aims to develop approaches that exhibit generalist behavior across diverse gripper designs. Existing methods often learn the gripper kinematic structure implicitly and face challenges due to the difficulty of sourcing the required large-scale data. In this work, we present a data-efficient, flow-based, equivariant grasp synthesis architecture that handles different gripper types with variable degrees of freedom and exploits the underlying kinematic model, deducing all necessary information solely from gripper and scene geometry. Unlike previous equivariant grasping methods, we implement all modules in JAX and provide batching capabilities over scenes, grippers, and grasps, resulting in smoother learning, improved performance, and faster inference. Our dataset encompasses grippers ranging from humanoid hands to parallel-jaw designs, including 25,000 scenes and 20 million grasps.

title: Intelligent Grasp Planning Using Open-Vocabulary Image Segmentation and Large Language Models
authors: Prithvi Raj Baskar; Bijo Sebastian; Alpana Dubey; Suma Mani Kuriakose
publication_title: 2025 IEEE 4th International Conference on Smart Technologies for Power, Energy and Control (STPEC)
abstract: Intelligent autonomous grasp planning is a key challenge in real-world deployment of robotic systems. Generating robust grasp require solving multiple challenges such perception, semantic segmentation, motion planning and grasp stability optimization. Over the years, many techniques have been proposed to solve one or more of the above challenges. Recent evolution of end-to-end learning for grasp planning has demonstrated the use of deep learning methods that map sensory data, such as images or point clouds, directly to grasp action. But these approaches require large datasets to train, and often struggle at sim-toreal transfer. Moreover the trained architecture is usually not interpretable and cannot guarantee safety or repeatability, which are important factors in real-world deployments. To address these limitations, we propose a novel grasp planning pipeline that can leverage the inference capability of Large Language Models, along with open vocabulary image segmentation. The depth image segmentation is further processed using classical algorithms that fit primitive shapes to the segmented point cloud data, resulting in stable grasp pose. The overall pipeline results in a repeatable and explainable pipeline for intelligent grasp generation, especially for everyday objects. The proposed pipeline was evaluated on two different scenes consisting everyday objects with varying clutter density. The pipeline was also compared with a data driven model on a set of standard shapes. Results indicate reliable grasp generation for everyday objects as well as comparable performance with the data driven approach on the standard set of objects.

title: MapleGrasp: Mask-guided Feature Pooling for Language-driven Efficient Robotic Grasping
authors: Vineet Bhat; Naman Patel; Prashanth Krishnamurthy; Ramesh Karri; Farshad Khorrami
publication_title: 2026 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
abstract: Robotic manipulation of unseen objects via natural language commands remains challenging. Language driven robotic grasping (LDRG) predicts stable grasp poses from natural language queries and RGB-D images. We propose MapleGrasp, a novel framework that leverages maskguided feature pooling for efficient vision-language driven grasping. Our two-stage training first predicts segmentation masks from CLIP-based vision-language features. The second stage pools features within these masks to generate pixel-level grasp predictions, improving efficiency, and reducing computation. Incorporating mask pooling results in a 7% improvement over prior approaches on the OCID-VLG benchmark. Furthermore, we introduce RefGraspNet, an open-source dataset larger than existing alternatives, significantly enhancing model generalization for open-vocabulary grasping. MapleGrasp scores a strong grasping accuracy of 89% when compared with competing methods in the RefGraspNet benchmark. Our method achieves comparable performance to larger Vision-Language-Action models on the LIBERO benchmark, and shows significantly better generalization to unseen tasks. Experiments on a Franka arm demonstrate 73% success rate with unseen objects, surpassing baselines by 11%. Code and dataset is available here: https://github.com/vineet2104/MapleGrasp.

title: START: Spatial and Textual Learning for Chart Understanding
authors: Zhuoming Liu; Xiaofeng Gao; Feiyang Niu; Qiaozi Gao; Liu Liu; Robinson Piramuthu
publication_title: 2026 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
abstract: Chart understanding is crucial for deploying multimodal large language models (MLLMs) in real-world scenarios such as analyzing scientific papers and technical reports. Unlike natural images, charts pair a structured visual layout (spatial property) with an underlying data representation (textual property) — grasping both is essential for precise, fine-grained chart reasoning. Motivated by this observation, we propose START, the Spatial and Textual learning for chART understanding. Specifically, we introduce (i) chart-element grounding and (ii) chart-to-code generation to strengthen an MLLM’s understanding of both chart visual layout and data details. To facilitate spatial and textual learning, we propose the START-Dataset generated with a novel data-generation pipeline that first leverages an MLLM to translate real chart images into executable chart code, recovering the underlying data representation while preserving the visual distribution of real-world charts. We then evolve the code with a Large Language Model (LLM) to ascertain the positions of chart elements that capture the chart’s visual structure, addressing challenges that existing methods cannot handle. To evaluate a model’s ability to understand chart spatial structures, we propose the Chart Spatial understanding Benchmark (CS-Bench), filling a critical gap in comprehensive chart understanding evaluation. Leveraging spatial and textual learning, START delivers consistent gains across model sizes and benchmarks over the base models and surpasses prior state-of-the-art by a clear margin. Code, data and models will be publicly available.

title: IEI-TIA: Industrial Embodied Intelligence Trustworthy Interpretable Agent for Robotic Long-Horizon and Repetitive Tasks
authors: Jiabao Dong; Lingyuan Yang; Pengji Fang; Shixiang Li; Yusheng Kong; Lei Ren
publication_title: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: With the rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence, embodied intelligence is increasingly being integrated into robotic tasks within smart manufacturing. Industrial operations typically feature long-horizon sequences and demand high precision. However, although embodied models, particularly Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, have shown significant promise in autonomous control with superior generalization capabilities, their inherent closed-box nature lacks the transparency and trustworthiness essential for manufacturing tasks. To address this challenge, we propose the Industrial Embodied Intelligence Trustworthy Interpretable Agent (IEI-TIA), a high-level trustworthy supervisory agent designed for industrial sorting and palletizing tasks. Rather than directly generating low-level control commands, IEI-TIA monitors robotic execution, diagnoses possible failure types at key operational stages, and provides corrective next-step instruction via invoked skills, thereby improving the reliability and interpretability of long-horizon and repetitive robotic tasks. An alignment-enhanced parameter-efficient finetuning method is proposed utilizing paired vision-language data to enable robust trustworthiness identification across various possible robotic failure types in different subtasks in sorting and palletizing. Additionally, we construct a specialized dataset and establish benchmarks for industrial embodied intelligence behavior diagnosis and instructions. Experimental results demonstrate that the fine-tuned trustworthy agent achieves 93.7% diagnosis accuracy for various task failures, representing a substantial improvement of approximately 38% over baseline general-purpose large models. By integrating the agent’s step-by-step operational instructions, the success rate of robotic long-horizon and repetitive tasks is improved by 14.0%. Note to Practitioners—This paper addresses a critical problem in industrial automation, the lack of interpretability and transparency of AI-driven robotic control in multi-stage and long-horizon tasks. In high-precision environments such as sorting or palletizing, AI closed-box models, including Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, often fail to provide safety guarantees required for manufacturing tasks, as minor execution errors can rapidly propagate and affect the entire sequence negatively. Therefore, we propose IEI-TIA, an autonomous supervisory agent that contributes to the shift from open-loop task execution to closed-loop trustworthy control with capability of providing diagnosis and instructions. Beyond identifying potential robotic failures like off-center grasps or misplaced parts, the agent also provides actionable next-step instructions that allow the embodied intelligence system to self-correct before errors escalate. A key practical advantage is that our industrial alignment-enhanced parameter-efficient finetuning (fine-tuning) method empowers the agent utilizing vision-language models with high failure-identification accuracy 93.7%, and corrective closed-loop logic without the need for retraining. The corresponding dataset and benchmarks offer a standardized framework for practitioners to evaluate and deploy interpretable embodied intelligence within existing automation pipelines. By implementing this agent, when using embodied intelligence models in manufacturing, factories can significantly reduce downtime caused by errors or mistakes made by untrustworthy AI robots, to achieve more robust and autonomous control in long-horizon robotic tasks.

title: Differentiable Inverse Graphics for Zero-Shot Scene Reconstruction and Robot Grasping
authors: Octavio Arriaga; Proneet Sharma; Jichen Guo; Marc Otto; Siddhant Kadwe; Rebecca Adam
publication_title: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Operating effectively in novel real-world environments requires robotic systems to estimate and interact with previously unseen objects. Current state-of-the-art models address this challenge by using large amounts of training data and test-time samples to build black-box scene representations. In this work, we introduce a differentiable neuro-graphics model that combines neural foundation models with physics-based differentiable rendering to perform zero-shot scene reconstruction and robot grasping without relying on any additional 3D data or test-time samples. Our model solves a series of constrained optimization problems to estimate physically consistent scene parameters, such as meshes, lighting conditions, material properties, and 6D poses of previously unseen objects from a single RGBD image and bounding boxes. We evaluated our approach on standard model-free few-shot benchmarks and demonstrated that it outperforms existing algorithms for model-free few-shot pose estimation. Furthermore, we validated the accuracy of our scene reconstructions by applying our algorithm to a zero-shot grasping task. By enabling zero-shot, physically-consistent scene reconstruction and grasping without reliance on extensive datasets or test-time sampling, our approach offers a pathway toward more data efficient, interpretable and generalizable robot autonomy in novel environments.

title: Research on adaptive operation of intelligent robotic arms based on SAC algorithm and hierarchical teaching
authors: Ying Meng; Chenglin Wang
publication_title: 7th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Manufacturing (AIAM 2025)
abstract: An adaptive operation model for intelligent robotic arms based on the integration of the Soft Actor–Critic (SAC) algorithm and hierarchical teaching is proposed. Building upon the existing reinforcement learning control framework, this model incorporates hierarchical teaching's high-level task decomposition and low-level action optimization mechanisms, establishing a comprehensive system spanning state modeling, reward function design, and policy execution. Experimental validation demonstrates that Hierarchical Demonstration Soft Actor–Critic (HD-SAC) achieves a 94.6% success rate in grasping and assembly tasks—approximately 11% higher than traditional SAC—while reducing energy consumption to 111.8 J and completion time to 16.2 s. Even under perturbed conditions, it maintains a success rate above 85% (with the highest reaching 89.3%) and lowers the collision rate to 4.3%, significantly outperforming baseline methods such as SAC and Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3). The results confirm that this method exhibits superior stability and robustness in complex tasks.

title: A Dual-arm Collaborative Manipulation Control Framework for Material Grasping
authors: Junbo Tan; Hengrong Zou; Guanqiu Guo; Fashan Sun; Xueqian Wang
publication_title: 2025 International Conference on Intelligent Manufacturing, Robotics and Automation (IMRA)
abstract: Dual-arm collaborative manipulation is essential for robots to perform complex tasks that mimic human dexterity in unstructured environments. We aim to build a practical framework that integrates perception, motion planning, and teleoperation for material grasping. Existing approaches often optimize a single module and struggle with dynamic scenes and human interaction. We propose a unified pipeline that couples You Only Look Once (YOLO)-based detection with Segment Anything Model (SAM) segmentation for accurate six degrees of freedom (6-DoF) pose estimation, a Rapidly-exploring Random Tree (RRT) planner operating in the composite joint space for collision-free bimanual trajectories, and an isomorphic master–slave teleoperation mode with direct joint mapping for difficult cases. This design preserves real-time performance while maintaining safety and precision. We further evaluate robustness in dynamic scenes involving moving distractors and human handovers. Across 30 trials for each condition, the system achieves a 90.0% grasp success rate in dynamic scenarios (96.7% in static tests), an average end-to-end perception latency of 85.3 ms, a mean 6-DoF pose error of 3.1 mm and 2.5°, and a mean motion planning time of 2.4 s, showing modest degradation under dynamic perturbations. The system completes human–robot handovers, autonomous tool grasping, and collaborative scooping across granular materials, providing a robust and reproducible solution aligned with the conference scope on perception–planning–control integration.

abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models empower robots to understand and execute tasks described by natural language instructions. However, a key challenge lies in their ability to generalize beyond the specific environments and conditions they were trained on, which is presently difficult and expensive to evaluate in the real-world. To address this gap, we present REALM, a new simulation environment and benchmark designed to evaluate the generalization capabilities of VLA models, with a specific emphasis on establishing a strong correlation between simulated and real-world performance through high-fidelity visuals and aligned robot control. Our environment offers a suite of 15 perturbation factors, 7 manipulation skills, and more than 3,500 objects. Finally, we establish two task sets that form our benchmark and evaluate the $\mathbf {\pi _{0}}$, $\mathbf {\pi _{0}}$-FAST, and GR00 T N1.5 VLA models, showing that generalization and robustness remain an open challenge. More broadly, we also show that simulation gives us a valuable proxy for the real-world and allows us to systematically probe for and quantify the weaknesses and failure modes of VLAs.

title: MediaPipe-based keyframe extraction method for hand grasping motions
authors: Hongyi Chen; Bo Song
publication_title: Jiangsu Annual Conference on Automation (JACA 2025)
abstract: To address the performance bottleneck of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in robotic arm imitation learning caused by context length constraints, this paper proposes a heuristic keyframe extraction method based on hand motion features. The method utilizes the MediaPipe hand keypoint detector to acquire hand motion trajectories, constructs a temporal hand velocity curve, and employs Gaussian filtering with local extremum detection strategies to identify velocity trough frames highly correlated with operations such as grasping and placing. To enhance robustness, a dual-threshold filtering mechanism is introduced, incorporating spatial confidence and temporal interval constraints to screen candidate keyframes. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a precision of 0.87 and an F1-Score of 0.88, significantly outperforming traditional uniform sampling approaches. This data-driven adaptive keyframe extraction strategy effectively preserves critical operational semantics while reducing redundant frames, providing a reliable visual context for subsequent VLM-based task reasoning and instruction generation.

title: VLA-Touch: Enhancing Vision-Language-Action Model With Dual-Level Tactile Feedback
authors: Jianxin Bi; Kevin Yuchen Ma; Ce Hao; Mike Shou Zheng; Harold Soh
publication_title: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Tactile feedback is generally recognized to be crucial for effective interaction with the physical world. However, state-of-the-art Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models often lack the ability to interpret and use tactile signals, limiting their effectiveness in contact-rich tasks. Incorporating tactile feedback into these systems is challenging due to the absence of large multi-modal datasets. We present VLA-Touch, an approach that enhances generalist robot policies with tactile sensing without fine-tuning the base VLA with tactile data. Our method introduces two key innovations: (1) a pipeline that leverages a pretrained tactile-language model to provide semantic tactile feedback for high-level task planning, and (2) a diffusion-based controller that refines VLA-generated actions with tactile signals for contact-rich manipulation. Through real-world experiments, we demonstrate that our dual-level integration of tactile feedback improves task planning success rate while enhancing execution precision.

title: Vision-Based Hand Shadowing for Robotic Manipulation via Inverse Kinematics
authors: Hendrik Chiche; Antoine Jamme; Trevor Rigoberto Martinez; Gabriel Gomes
publication_title: IEEE Access
abstract: Teleoperation of low-cost robotic manipulators remains challenging due to the difficulty of retargeting human hand motion to robot joint commands. We present an offline hand-shadowing inverse-kinematics (IK) retargeting pipeline driven by a single egocentric RGB-D camera mounted on 3D-printed glasses. The pipeline detects 21 hand landmarks per hand using MediaPipe Hands, deprojects them into 3D via depth sensing, transforms them into the robot coordinate frame, and solves a damped-least-squares IK problem to produce joint commands for the SO-ARM101 robot (5 arm + 1 gripper joints). A gripper controller maps thumb–index finger geometry to grasp aperture with a multi-level fallback hierarchy. Actions are previewed in a physics simulation before replay on the physical robot. We evaluate the pipeline on a structured pick-and-place benchmark (5-tile grid, 10 grasps per tile, 3 independent runs) achieving an  $86.7\% \pm 4.2\%$  success rate, and compare it against four vision-language-action (VLA) policies (ACT, SmolVLA,  $\pi _{0.5}$ , GR00T N1.5) trained on leader–follower teleoperation data. We provide a quantitative error analysis of the pipeline, reporting a mean IK position error of 36.4 mm, trajectory smoothness metrics showing 57–68% jerk reduction from EMA smoothing, and an ablation study over the smoothing parameter. We also test the pipeline in unstructured real-world environments (grocery store, pharmacy) and find that success is reduced to 9.3% due to hand occlusion by surrounding objects. To mitigate this, we integrate WiLoR as an alternative hand detector, achieving an 8% improvement in hand detection rate over MediaPipe, highlighting both the promise and current limitations of marker-free analytical retargeting.

title: State Space Modeling of User Intent Drift for Confidence-Calibrated News Recommendation
authors: N M Vedhinee; Rajalakshmi D; Janisa Ria; Prakratee Singh
publication_title: 2026 3rd International Conference on Research Methodologies in Knowledge Management, Artificial Intelligence and Telecommunication Engineering (RMKMATE)
abstract: News Article suggestion models these days often rely on user click histories that are based on static preference estimates without any measure of the confidence level of their recommendations. Problems arise when user interests change dynamically, and their news article recommendations are not aligned with their preferences. We aim to tackle this situation with the help of the State Space Model (SSM) using Large Language Model (LLM) that keeps a hidden state, which tracks evolving user interest and preference changes over time. Using the MIND dataset, the LLM grasps the meaning of the new articles and stores them as dense vectors. Along with this, the user's progress as well as their changes in articles of interest are tracked using SSM's hidden state. While traditional recommendation engines show you articles ranked by relevance alone, our model additionally includes a second dimension: quantifying how confident it is about its recommendation. This shift reduces the over-confidence in the model's predictions, which proves valuable for readers with sporadic changes in topics of interest. By building uncertainty into the engine itself, our goal is to recommend news articles to users without hiding how the choices were made, even when new trends emerge rapidly.

title: SLAP: Slapband-Based Autonomous Perching Drone with Failure Recovery for Vertical Tree Trunks
authors: Julia Di; Kenneth A. W. Hoffmann; Tony G. Chen; Tian-Ao Ren; Mark Cutkosky
publication_title: 2026 IEEE Aerospace Conference
abstract: Perching allows unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to reduce energy consumption, remain anchored for surface sampling operations, or stably survey their surroundings. Previous efforts for perching on vertical surfaces have predominantly focused on lightweight mechanical design solutions with relatively scant system-level integration. Furthermore, perching strategies for vertical surfaces commonly require high-speed, aggressive landing operations that are dangerous for a surveyor drone with sensitive electronics onboard. This work presents the preliminary investigation of a perching approach suitable for larger drones that both gently perches on vertical tree trunks and reacts and recovers from perch failures. The system in this work, called SLAP, consists of vision-based perch site detector, an IMU (inertial-measurement-unit)-based perch failure detector, an attitude controller for soft perching, an optical close-range detection system, and a fast active elastic gripper with microspines made from commercially-available slapbands. We validated this approach on a modified 1.2 kg commercial quadrotor with component and system analysis. Initial human-in-the-loop autonomous indoor flight experiments achieved a 75% perch success rate on a real oak tree segment across 20 flights, and 100 % perch failure recovery across 2 flights with induced failures. Videos and code of flight tests can be found at our project website: https://slap-perching.github.io/.

title: Fast and Efficient 6-DoF Grasp Estimation With Segment Anything Model in Cluttered Scenes
authors: Sheng Yu; Di-Hua Zhai; Yuanqing Xia
publication_title: IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics
abstract: The task of executing object grasping in unstructured and cluttered environments is a significant challenge. Despite the development of various 6-DoF grasping methods to tackle this issue, rapid grasping objects from arbitrary viewpoints remains difficult. In this article, we introduce a zero-shot 6-DoF grasp pose estimation method for unstructured cluttered scenes, named FS-Grasp. Initially, we leverage the zero-shot capabilities of the segment anything model to perform object segmentation in cluttered scenes, thereby obtaining point clouds of unknown objects. Next, we design a zero-shot 6-DoF grasp pose prediction algorithm based on these object point clouds, enabling the detection of grasp poses for unknown objects in cluttered environments. In FS-Grasp, we introduce a multiscale, multiangle graspable region search algorithm that integrates transformers to conduct a comprehensive search for graspable poses. We conduct grasping tests across various datasets, and our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed FS-Grasp can be effectively applied to most zero-shot grasping tasks. Furthermore, we apply FS-Grasp in diverse human–robot interaction scenarios, establishing an autonomous robot grasping framework based on visual language large models, which successfully performs the grasping and placement of multiple unknown objects, showcasing considerable practical application value.

title: Think Before You Leap: A Robot Task Planning Method By LLM
authors: Zhibin Yang; Zhi Zheng
publication_title: 2025 Asian Conference on Artificial Intelligence Technology (ACAIT)
abstract: The integration of Large Language Model (LLM) with robotic arm grasping systems represents a key focus in embodied intelligence. However, in long-sequence complex task planning, inaccurate user requirements and intricate constraints pose significant challenges to LLM’s reasoning capabilities. Conventional simple prompts fail to help LLM accurately interpret user needs or generate effective task plans. To address this, we propose a robot manipulation task planning framework that combines chain-of-thought reasoning, self-reflection, and LLM to ensure the correctness and feasibility of generated plans. The framework operates in three stages: (1) Preprocessing, where an LLM translator converts natural language into planning domain definition language; (2) Planning, where an LLM planner creates an initial plan and enables self-reflection through autonomous evaluation and iterative refinement; (3) Execution, where an encoder translates language-based plans into executable Python code. MUJOCO simulation experiments demonstrate our method’s superior robustness and accuracy in robotic object sorting and block-world tasks compared to state-of-the-art approaches, achieving 30% and 34% higher success rates in two scenarios.

title: VLM as a Virtual Proprioception: Semantic Slip Detection for Sensorless Grippers Using Quantized Small-Scale Models
authors: Chacharin Lertyosbordin; Boonyawat Chaithirasakul; Puvasit Aphisinrungrot; Sorathon Chungsawanant; Nontapat Prayoonthong

abstract: Reliable manipulation in unstructured environments typically requires expensive force-torque sensors to detect grasping failures. Low-cost robotic arms, relying on open-loop control, lack this proprioceptive feedback, rendering them susceptible to slippage and “air delivery” errors-particularly when handling small objects with dimensional variances. This paper introduces “Virtual Proprioception,” a framework that repurposes a quantized Vision-Language Model (VLM), specifically Qwen3-VL-4B, as a semantic tactile sensor. To circumvent the inference latency inherent in large models, we propose a Discrete Keyframe Monitoring strategy that utilizes semantic reasoning to verify object presence at four critical state transitions. The system was validated using a specialized test set of 3D-printed components fabricated with ± 2 mm manufacturing tolerances. Experimental results demonstrate that while the baseline open-loop system suffered a 35.0% Critical Failure Rate due to undetected slippage, our proposed framework successfully intercepted all failure instances, reducing the Critical Failure Rate to 0%. These findings confirm that lightweight VLMs can effectively serve as software-defined alternatives to hardware sensors, democratizing high-reliability manipulation for resource-constrained robotics.

title: Reconstructing Hand-Held Objects in 3D from Images and Videos
authors: Jane Wu; Georgios Pavlakos; Georgia Gkioxari; Jitendra Malik
publication_title: 2026 International Conference on 3D Vision (3DV)
abstract: Objects manipulated by the hand (i.e., manipulanda) are particularly challenging to reconstruct from Internet videos. Not only does the hand occlude much of the object, but also the object is often only visible in a small number of image pixels. At the same time, two strong anchors emerge in this setting: (1) estimated 3D hands help disambiguate the location and scale of the object, and (2) the set of manipulanda is small relative to all possible objects. With these insights in mind, we present a scalable paradigm for hand-held object reconstruction that builds on recent breakthroughs in large language/vision models and 3D object datasets. Given a monocular RGB video, we aim to reconstruct hand-held object geometry in 3D, over time. In order to obtain the best performing single frame model, we first present MCC-Hand-Object (MCCHO), which jointly reconstructs hand and object geometry given a single RGB image and inferred 3D hand as inputs. Subsequently, we prompt a text-to-3D generative model using a VLM to retrieve a 3D object model that matches the object in the image(s); we call this alignment Retrieval-Augmented Reconstruction (RAR). RAR provides unified object geometry across all frames, and the result is rigidly aligned with both the input images and 3D MCCHO observations in a temporally consistent manner. Experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-theart performance on lab and Internet image/video datasets. We make our code and models available on the project website: https://janehwu.github.io/mcc-ho

title: Follow My Hold: Hand-Object Interaction Reconstruction Through Geometric Guidance
authors: Ayce Idil Aytekin; Helge Rhodin; Rishabh Dabral; Christian Theobalt

abstract: We propose a novel diffusion-based framework for reconstructing 3D geometry of hand-held objects from monocular RGB images by leveraging hand-object interaction as geometric guidance. Our method conditions a latent diffusion model on an inpainted object appearance and uses inference-time guidance to optimize the object reconstruction, while simultaneously ensuring plausible hand-object interactions. Unlike prior methods that rely on extensive post-processing or produce low-quality reconstructions, our approach directly generates high-quality object geometry during the diffusion process by introducing guidance with an optimization-in-the-loop design. Specifically, we guide the diffusion model by applying supervision to the velocity field while simultaneously optimizing the transformations of both the hand and the object being reconstructed. This optimization is driven by multi-modal geometric cues, including normal and depth alignment, silhouette consistency, and 2D keypoint reprojection. We further incorporate signed distance field supervision and enforce contact and non-intersection constraints to ensure physical plausibility of hand-object interaction. Our method yields accurate, robust and coherent reconstructions under occlusion while generalizing well to in-the-wild scenarios. title: A Large Language Model-Based Game Equilibrium Selection Approach for Human-Machine Shared Driving
authors: Yi Yang; Chunyue Song; Huang Li; Jun Zhao
publication_title: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
abstract: Human-machine shared driving (HMSD) has emerged as a crucial transitional paradigm before the widespread adoption of fully autonomous vehicles. However, existing research typically only considers either human-dominated or human-machine equal relationships, neglecting the fact that these two relationships alternate during driving, which leads to a gap between theory and reality. To address this issue, this study proposes a large language model (LLM)-based game equilibrium selection approach for human-machine shared driving authority allocation. Firstly, a game equilibrium selection model is developed to seamlessly transition between Stackelberg equilibrium and Nash equilibrium, addressing human-dominated and human-machine equal relationships, respectively. The selection process is implemented using an LLM, which bases its decisions on scenario understanding. To enhance the LLM’s scenario understanding performance, a set of indicators capturing human-machine conflicts, driver involvement, and collision risks is introduced as prior knowledge. Furthermore, an LLM-based scenario-understanding module is designed to embed knowledge into the LLM and enable it to function effectively within the HMSD system. Finally, a human-in-the-loop experiment is conducted to validate the proposed strategy. The results show that LLMs can understand the provided knowledge, flexibly adapt to different scenarios, and accurately grasp human-machine interactions. Moreover, the proposed strategy effectively reduces human-machine conflicts, better satisfies driver intentions, and reduces driver workload, showcasing the potential of LLM-based decision-making in human-machine interaction.

abstract: This paper presents an end-to-end robotic infrastructure for deploying vision-language-action (VLA) models on the open-source BCN3D Moveo robot arm. The approach combines a ROS2-based real-time control stack, a high-fidelity digital twin in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, a LeRobot-formatted dataset converted from RLDS, and efficient fine-tuning strategies for the GROOT 1.5 foundation model. The proposed framework targets low-cost manipulation with a single RGB camera while addressing sim-to-real transfer, generalization to unseen objects, and data scarcity. An ablation study over training data volume (39 vs. 47 episodes) and fine-tuning epoch depth shows that richer task variation shifts the optimal checkpoint from mid- to late-stage training, yielding a 7.8 % improvement in offline MSE. Comparative fine-tuning experiments further reveal that backbone LoRA training for GR00T and $\pi_{0}$ is blocked by HuggingFace Transformers incompatibilities, while OpenVLA full fine-tuning fails due to out-of-memory constraints. Offline action-space error analysis reports MSE, RMSE, and MAE values of $0.1073,0.3275$, and 0.1523, respectively.

abstract: For a robot to autonomously perform physical manipulation tasks, it must be capable of reasoning about how to execute them and determining specific behaviors based on its joint states and environmental perception. In this work, the reasoning process is modeled through a Large Language Model (LLM) that decomposes high-level task descriptions into ordered sub-tasks, each associated—via embeddings—with behavioral data collected from a 6-DOF serial robot performing object manipulation. This study analyzes the structure and dimensionality of the sub-task sequences generated by different LLMs to identify which configuration best aligns with the dynamic data of the robot's physical behavior. The ultimate goal is to enable scalable reasoning-action coupling for robots operating within intelligent environments, such as educational, industrial, or assistive settings—where adaptability and task automation are essential.

title: ATP-VLA: A Robust Grasping Framework Driven by Temporal Asymmetric Multimodal Fusion and Representation Isomorphism
authors: Haocong Duan; Guangsen Xue; Jinyan Zhang; Meile Zhu; Zhongwei Zhao
publication_title: IEEE Access
abstract: Existing vision-language-action (VLA) models are highly susceptible to “visual hallucinations” when manipulating deceptive objects, whereas introducing high-energy tactile verification inherently risks “perception-as-destruction.” In this paper, we propose the Acoustic-Tactile Perception Vision-Language-Action (ATP-VLA) framework, a robust grasping framework based on temporal asymmetric multimodal fusion. First, we introduce a Representation Isomorphism mechanism that unifies and projects 1D transient contact sounds and 3D tactile indentations into 2D visual tokens, effectively bridging the semantic gap across heterogeneous sensors. Second, we construct a Dynamic Bayesian Decision Tree following a progressive belief-update logic: “visual prior—low-energy acoustic probing—high-energy tactile verification.” This cascaded routing mechanism triggers tactile sensing only upon detecting cross-modal confidence conflicts, achieving a global balance between computational cost and physical damage risk. Experiments on standard benchmarks (e.g., ObjectFolder Real) and our custom deceptive adversarial dataset demonstrate that ATP-VLA not only achieves a high decision matching rate of 88.8%, but also exhibits a strong Conservative Safety Bias under dynamic temporal routing, effectively reducing the physical damage rate to 3.9%. Furthermore, through extreme adversarial probing, we reveal the Structural Hallucination limitations inherent in current VLA models, validating the necessity of an external temporal routing mechanism to ensure system safety. Finally, by demonstrating the positive correlation between acoustic attenuation and tactile deformation, we validate the physical interpretability of the system’s decision-making process.

title: Dual-Layer Adaptive Filtering and Asynchronous Trajectory Interpolation for Low-Cost Robotic Manipulators
authors: Zihan Chen; Jingyi Ou; Wenbo Zhu; Yiran He; Wei Yu; Haibing Li; Haowen Tang
publication_title: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent Perception and Autonomous Control (IPAC)
abstract: With the rise of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) large language models, embodied intelligence has demonstrated immense potential in complex manipulation tasks. However, the challenge of reliably deploying high-frequency policy outputs onto low-cost serial servo hardware remains a core bottleneck hindering the widespread adoption of robotics. Traditional methods, such as direct command issuance or smoothing techniques relying on internal servo registers, often face a trade-off between suppressing mechanical resonance (jitter) and avoiding phase lag, leading to uncontrollable oscillations in the end-effector and subsequently disrupting the visual feedback loop. To address this challenge, inspired by the concept of control decoupling, this paper proposes a two-layer adaptive mapping architecture. In the upper-level spatial domain, by cascading exponential moving averages (EMA) with nonlinear dead-zone clipping, the method eliminates strategy noise at the source and constructs a static freezing window to optimize the visual capture environment; in the lower-level temporal domain, the introduction of asynchronous-independent threads executing high-frequency linear interpolation effectively bridges the discrete gap between model inference and low-level execution. Experiments show this reduces mechanical jitter by 18.8% and boosts grasping success from 65% to 80%, providing a highly scalable paradigm for the robust deployment of embodied intelligence on budget-friendly hardware.

title: FreMotion: A Frequency-Motion Synergy Framework for Imitation Learning in Robust Robotic Fine Manipulation
authors: Jie Mei; Xinkai Wu; Yue Zhang; Tao Song; Zhongxia Xiong
publication_title: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: Imitation learning has emerged as a promising paradigm for automating robotic fine manipulation, yet maintaining temporal coherence and execution precision in long-horizon tasks remains a formidable challenge. This requires addressing exponential error accumulation in long-horizon tasks, as well as the inherent trade-off between millimeter-level positioning precision and motion smoothness, which is critical for the stability and accuracy of robotic automation systems. To this end, we propose FreMotion, a task-driven asymmetric encoder-decoder framework designed to enhance the robustness and efficiency of robotic manipulation. Our approach introduces the Temporal Dynamic Encoder (TDE-Net), which employs linear attention with dynamic gating to capture long-range dependencies and mitigate error accumulation in continuous control. Simultaneously, the Frequency-Aware Decoder (FAD-Net) leverages a dual-path attention mechanism to explicitly disentangle and fuse high- and low-frequency information for precise visuo-motor coordination. Extensive experiments on bimanual robotic tasks demonstrate that FreMotion, with orders of magnitude fewer parameters (approx. 100M vs. Billions), not only outperforms state-of-the-art Vision-Language-Action (VLA) methods in success rate but also achieves faster inference time, thus ensuring high-frequency continuous control required for industrial automation. Note to Practitioners—This paper addresses the challenge of automating fine manipulation tasks, such as precision assembly, where current data-driven methods often produce jittery controls that cause actuator wear and failure. We present FreMotion, a robust imitation learning framework that achieves millimeter-level precision without expensive specialized sensors. By decoupling control signals into low-frequency trends (for motion smoothness) and high-frequency signals (for accuracy), our system enables standard robotic arms to perform complex bimanual tasks effectively. Experimental results confirm FreMotion meets the low-latency inference constraints critical for fluid bimanual operations. Practitioners should note the current system relies on task-specific expert demonstrations; future work will reduce data requirements and improve adaptability to new object geometries.

title: MDM-Grasp: Learning Grasp Stability With a Two-Phase, Multimodal Framework
authors: Ke Zhang; Pengwen Xiong; Xiaocong Li; Aiguo Song
publication_title: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics
abstract: Accurate grasp stability assessment is essential for reliable robotic manipulation. However, most approaches treat grasping as a static action, overlooking dynamic challenges from multistage interactions, sensor noise, and the lack of physical commonsense. To address these limitations, we propose multistage dynamic multi-modal grasp (MDM-Grasp), a framework for grasp stability assessment. The framework employs a cascaded two-phase architecture that integrates spatiotemporal tactile sequences, visual inputs, and prior physical knowledge extracted from a large language model (LLM). To enhance robustness under realistic conditions, we introduce a mutual cross-attention fusion mechanism (MCFM) for effective integration of heterogeneous and noisy sensory streams. We further construct a comprehensive dataset encompassing diverse lighting, object, and sensor degradation conditions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MDM-Grasp achieves state-of-the-art performance, with F1-scores of 99.19% in the initial assessment phase and 96.57% in the refinement phase and generalizes well to unseen objects with a 96.67% real-world success rate. These results highlight the potential of combining multimodal sensing with language-model-based priors to enable more reliable and human-like robotic grasping in complex environments.

title: Depth-Enhanced Dual-Arm Visual Servoing for Texture-Less Fabric Alignment
authors: Anyu Lou; Lu Chen; Zhongxiang Zhou; Chengguang Wang; Genke Yang; Rong Xiong; Hongxiang Yu
publication_title: 2026 38th Chinese Control and Decision Conference (CCDC)
abstract: Manipulating deformable objects like fabrics presents significant challenges in robotics due to their infinite degrees of freedom, self-occlusions, and texture-less surfaces. Traditional monocular visual servoing methods often suffer from scale-depth ambiguity, where the visual contraction caused by fabric wrinkling is misinterpreted as an increase in depth, leading to erroneous control actions along the optical axis. To address this, we propose a geometry-aware dual-arm visual servoing framework that explicitly fuses depth information to resolve geometric uncertainties. By stacking RGB and Depth features, our network learns to decouple intrinsic deformation from rigid body motion, outputting synchronized dual-arm end-effector velocities to align the cloth with a visual target. We employ a DAgger-style imitation learning strategy, initialized by a position-based expert policy with motion clamping to ensure safety and prevent overstretching. The proposed approach is validated in both simulation and real-world environments. Experimental results demonstrate that the inclusion of depth constraints significantly enhances robustness against illumination changes and deformation ambiguities, achieving high-precision cloth positioning.

title: Vision-Guided Recovery: Enhancing Robotic Manipulation through Intelligent Failure Detection
authors: Vladimir Sivtsov; Daniil Shkolnik; Muslim Alaran; Athanasios Papanikolaou; Enrica Zereik; Ivan Petrovic; Fabio Bonsignorio
publication_title: 2026 IEEE Engineering Reliable Autonomous Systems (ERAS)
abstract: Vision-language-based robotic learning of manipulation remains a significant challenge despite remarkable advances. While vision-language large models have shown impressive capabilities and interesting emerging behaviors, they still often struggle, especially when encountering failures during performance. The lack of the ability to reflect on their errors is a challenge that hinders a transition to truly intelligent and reliable embodied agents. We present a new framework that addresses this crucial limitation by continuous analysis of visual data of the task performance of the robot by a multimodal large language model. It predicts whether the robot performs well or has difficulties and, if necessary, automatically initiates a backtracking procedure that allows it to re-approach the task without human intervention. Experiments conducted on the ManiSkill3 platform with the manipulation benchmarks show that this approach increases task success rates by up to 2 times compared to standard vision-language models. This work bridges the gap between imitation learning-based large foundational models for manipulation and self-reflective correction as a step towards more reliable autonomous systems.

title: SAGA: Open-World Mobile Manipulation via Structured Affordance Grounding
authors: Kuan Fang; Yuxin Chen; Xinghao Zhu; Farzad Niroui; Lingfeng Sun; Jiuguang Wang
publication_title: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: We present SAGA, a versatile and adaptive framework for visuomotor control that can generalize across various environments, task objectives, and user specifications. To efficiently learn such capability, our key idea is to disentangle high-level semantic intent from low-level visuomotor control by explicitly grounding task objectives in the observed environment. Using an affordance-based task representation, we express diverse and complex behaviors in a unified, structured form. By leveraging multimodal foundation models, SAGA grounds the proposed task representation to the robot's visual observation as 3D affordance heatmaps, highlighting task-relevant entities while abstracting away spurious appearance variations that would hinder generalization. These grounded affordances enable us to effectively train a conditional policy on multi-task demonstration data for whole-body control. In a unified framework, SAGA can solve tasks specified in different forms, including language instructions, selected points, and example demonstrations, enabling both zero-shot execution and few-shot adaptation. We instantiate SAGA on a quadrupedal manipulator and conduct extensive experiments across eleven real-world tasks. SAGA consistently outperforms end-to-end and modular baselines by substantial margins. Together, these results demonstrate that structured affordance grounding offers a scalable and effective pathway toward generalist mobile manipulation.

abstract: Behavior-cloning-based visuomotor policies enable precise manipulation but often inherit the slow, cautious tempo of human demonstrations, limiting practical deployment. title: Adaptive Closed-Loop Robotic Grasping via Causal Reasoning and Hierarchical Meta-Reinforcement Learning
authors: Yunwei Zhang; Jing Tian; Chengjin Tao; Zhongxin Ma; Bin Li

abstract: Robotic grasping and manipulation in unstructured environments remains a fundamental challenge for embodied intelligence. Current approaches face a dilemma. End-to-end reinforcement learning offers adaptability but suffers from low sample efficiency and opaque decision-making. Rule-based systems, in contrast, provide stability but lack flexibility. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a hybrid autonomous decision-making framework that synergizes interpretable Causal Inference with sample-efficient Hierarchical Meta-Reinforcement Learning (HMRL). A key innovation of our approach is the utilization of causal inference to perform interpretable diagnostics on grasping failures. These diagnostics generate structured intervention signals that guide the hierarchical meta-policy for rapid online adaptation. In doing so, the framework simultaneously enhances decision transparency, improves failure recovery efficiency, and supports cross-task generalization. We integrate these components into a complete “perception-diagnosis-decision-execution” closed-loop system, incorporating a confidence-based rule fallback mechanism to ensure operational safety. Extensive experiments in simulation demonstrate that our system outperforms baseline methods in cluttered and densely packed scenarios. It achieves a 5–13% improvement in task completion rates and shows superior capability in recovering from execution failures.

title: Phase-Conditioned Imitation Learning With Autonomous Failure Recovery for Robust Deformable Object Manipulation
authors: Dayuan Chen; Kai Tang; Yukuan Zhang; Kazuhiro Kosuge; Yasuhisa Hirata
publication_title: IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics
abstract: In this article, we present a phase-conditioned, force-aware framework for robust deformable object manipulation. Standard imitation learning policies, such as action chunking with transformers (ACT), rely on a Markovian assumption at inference, causing state aliasing when visually similar observations require contradictory actions and preventing autonomous recovery from execution failures. We address this with a closed-loop hierarchical architecture. A Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM)-conditioned ACT encoder modulates feature extraction based on the current task phase, enabling a single unified policy to produce phase-specific behaviors while sharing action dynamics across phases. A multimodal phase predictor fusing visual, force, and pose feedback estimates the phase in real time, detecting contact failures that are invisible to vision alone and autonomously triggering recovery trajectories. The system is completed by a hybrid impedance controller for compliant execution and a haptic teleoperation interface for force-aware data collection. Ablation studies show that FiLM-based modulation significantly outperforms both unconditioned and token-level conditioned baselines, and t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding analysis confirms that FiLM induces well-separated, phase-specific feature representations. Validated on hanging and removing a T-shirt with dual arms, the closed-loop system improves the hanging success rate from 56% to 87% through autonomous error recovery.

title: FIRE-Grasp: Failure-Informed Regrasping With Multimodal Evidence
authors: Bojun Yang; Yifan Sun; Yilin Huang; Ye Lin; Junling Wang; Yi Guo
publication_title: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Robotic grasping represents a fundamental capability for autonomous manipulation, yet real-world deployments continue to exhibit significant failure rates, undermining operational reliability. Ensuring operational continuity and minimizing risk necessitate effective failure recovery mechanisms, making regrasping after grasp failure a critical capability. Prior approaches either operate in an open-loop manner that ignores post-failure recovery or develop multimodal failure perception models that fail to translate diagnostic insights into executable regrasp actions. Consequently, a persistent gap exists between the rich multimodal evidence captured during execution and the low-level, actionable decisions required for reliable regrasping in real-world deployments. In this paper, we propose FIRE-Grasp (Failure-Informed Regrasping with multimodal Evidence), a closed-loop regrasping framework that converts first-attempt multimodal failure feedback into executable regrasp corrections, which comprises (i) FIRE-Net, a multimodal failure diagnosis network that outputs a structured Failure Feedback Vector encoding both the predicted failure type and temporally localized event evidence, along with global reliability estimates; and (ii) FIRE-Adapter, which maps FFV to planner-consumable corrections via risk-aware candidate re-ranking and conservative low-dimensional execution-parameter updates. To enable fine-grained failure diagnosis, FailGrasp, a real-world dataset of 2,428 grasp failure trials with synchronized vision, force/torque, and audio across five failure categories is established. On FailGrasp, FIRE-Net achieves 88.12% top-1 accuracy and 87.41% macro-F1. Real-robot experiments further demonstrate that FIRE-Grasp improves grasp recovery after failure, achieving 80.56% regrasp success rate, 89.17% completion rate within 3 attempts, and 96.67% completion rate within 5 attempts.

title: FG-CLTP: Fine-Grained Contrastive Language Tactile Pretraining for Robotic Manipulation
authors: Wenxuan Ma; Chaofan Zhang; Yinghao Cai; Guocai Yao; Shaowei Cui; Shuo Wang
publication_title: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
abstract: Recent advancements in integrating tactile sensing into vision-language-action (VLA) models have demonstrated transformative potential for robotic perception. However, existing tactile representations predominantly rely on qualitative descriptors (e.g., texture), neglecting quantitative contact states such as force magnitude, contact geometry, and principal axis orientation, which are indispensable for fine-grained manipulation. To bridge this gap, we propose FG-CLTP, a fine-grained contrastive language tactile pretraining framework. We first introduce a novel dataset comprising over 100 k tactile 3D point cloud-language pairs that explicitly capture multidimensional contact states from the sensor’s perspective. We then implement a discretized numerical tokenization mechanism to achieve quantitative-semantic alignment, effectively injecting explicit physical metrics into the multimodal feature space. The proposed FG-CLTP model yields a 95.9% classification accuracy and reduces the regression error (MAE) by 52.6% compared to state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, the integration of 3D point cloud representations establishes a sensor-agnostic foundation with a minimal sim-to-real gap of 3.5%. Building upon this fine-grained representation, we develop a 3D tactile-language-action (3D-TLA) architecture driven by a flow matching policy to enable multimodal reasoning and control. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our framework significantly outperforms strong baselines in contact-rich manipulation tasks, providing a robust and generalizable foundation for tactile-language-action models.

title: Open-Set Object Detection for Future HRI: Enabling Natural Language Commands for Robotic Control in Unstructured Industrial Environments
authors: Richard Schwarz; Ali Muhammad; Oto Haffner; Danica Rosinová
publication_title: IEEE Access
abstract: This paper proposes a modular zero-programming robotic manipulation system that enables robotic arms to execute natural language instructions in unstructured environments. The proposed approach integrates lightweight Natural Language Processing (NLP), open-set object detection, and monocular depth estimation to interpret user commands and compute grasp poses using only a robot (UR10e and xArm 6) and a single overhead camera. Our solution integrates several pretrained neural network models. SpaCy is used to extract the task structure from the language, GroundingDINO provides text-conditioned open-set object detection without retraining, and DepthAnythingV2 combined with contour analysis and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) provides an analytical method for determining the optimal grasp-angle based on object contours. A functional workspace-segmentation method mitigates the stringency of fixed camera calibration by accommodating slight spatial variations. Experiments on diverse objects demonstrate promising detection accuracy, functional grasp-pose estimation, and demonstrate the feasibility of executing move, remove, and rotate actions. The results show that the designed modular foundation-model pipeline can provide interpretable, flexible, and hardware-efficient instruction-driven manipulation also for non-expert users.

title: A Lightweight Modular Vision-Language-Action Framework for Real-Time Closed-Loop Robotic Manipulation
authors: Minghao Lou; Guangxin Zhang; Yuansheng Wu; Zhijie Jian; Taotao Liang; Jiehao Li; Guangrong Chen
publication_title: 2026 41st Youth Academic Annual Conference of Chinese Association of Automation (YAC)
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) large models enable advanced cross-modal perception for robotic manipulators, but real-world deployment is limited by semantic alignment errors, sim-to-real gaps, poor manipulation robustness, and high hardware costs. This paper proposes a lightweight, modular VLA-driven control framework for 6-DOF robotic manipulators, with natural language instructions and visual perception as dual inputs. A closed-loop three-layer "perception-decision-control" architecture maps multi-modal inputs to physical actions without end-to-end training or VLA fine-tuning. The perception layer fuses RealSense D455 RGB/depth data via improved YOLOv8 for accurate target detection and 3D pose estimation. The decision layer leverages DeepSeek VLA to parse commands, align cross-modal semantics, and generate parameterized actions. The control layer converts commands into collision-free joint trajectories (DH kinematics/Lagrangian dynamics) and drives a Ti5 dexterous hand with impedance force control for fine-grained manipulation. Experiments on a self-built platform validate robust execution of single/multi-step instructions for grasping rigid/fragile/irregular objects in complex occluded scenes, achieving 98% recognition accuracy, ±3mm coordinate error, more than 95% grasping success rate, and less than 2s end-to-end latency. This work demonstrates that structured cross-modal fusion and modular design enable effective VLA integration, eliminating traditional pipeline fragmentation, and provides a low-cost, reliable solution for intelligent manipulator upgrades in manufacturing, service robotics, and agriculture.
